decisions: Random frozen adapter is an engineering benchmark-adapted representation, not a trained or pretrained ResNet claim.

PA selects on the generated pu_val view by proxy accuracy (Wang et al. 2026 Definition 1, OS branch) over the same per-checkpoint val-side min-max threshold grid OA uses; the population class prior pi is required per run (from the run's class_prior, else the split artifact's class_prior.population) and a run without it fails loudly. Formal SCAR PA acceptance remains pending the collaborator's signature.

KLDCE binds flip_probability = 1 - c for SCAR only and is rebuilt for each c; all SAR requests are rejected. Its execution rows still require approved protocol and dataset-specific budget/resource gates.
Self-PU uses two sampled optimizer steps per epoch, not a full traversal, and has no budget-matched mini-batch oracle; its comparability group is separate.
selection_spec is descriptive documentation; runner behavior is enforced by code and checkpoint tests, not by dynamically consuming this prose field.
Implementing the PA criterion does not by itself unblock the pre-registered PA units: the 54 blocked_pending_pa_criterion mappings stay blocked until the P2.0c review rules on them.
Sampling-assumption adjudication follows the paper first; the reference code is used only when the paper is silent, and paper/code differences are registered.
Native-TS methods use TS-compatible calibration (D_U <- D_U union D_P) on OS data; this is not TS data resampling.
The canonical prior is population pi; pi_U = pi under the ts view and pi_U = (pi*n - n_L)/(n - n_L) under the SCAR os view.
Architecture exceptions are limited to architectures or recipes required by the method mechanism or the paper; author-code implementation choices are not exceptions.
The main table defaults to PA selection; OA configurations are recorded for reference (Q2).
Architecture-exception methods remain single-listed; a shared-architecture comparison run SHOULD be provided when feasible, and its absence is noted in the result table/method card (Q1).
PA+clean-support results are listed in the same SCAR-PA table with an explicit annotation and are excluded from pure-PU PA advantage comparisons (Q3).

Training-time clean support is required by PULNS, LaGAM, and the full Self-PU branch; the no-clean Self-PU path is an explicit ablation. Support is disjoint from the remaining train, pu_val, clean_val, and test; this round carves it from train and removes it, sized 100 for Spambase and 500 otherwise, and its positive and negative labels count toward the training-time label budget (approved 2026-10-21).
This round covers Spambase, Connect-4, MNIST, F-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 only; IMDB, 20News, and ADNI are excluded from PA+clean-support.

The formal PA+clean-support runner is a P3.2 implementation gate; until it lands, only OA clean-support results are reported. Existing self_pu execution units retain the no-meta ablation profile; full Self-PU rows require new clean-support units in P3.2.
method_profiles.self_pu remains the explicit no-meta ablation profile used by the frozen pilot; the full clean-meta variant will use a separate profile and units when the P3.2 support runner lands.
